To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) We have shown that a pulsed optical carrier injection can induce a large frequency detuning of the fundamental mode in a GaAs micropillars.
we have demonstrated a new method to generate ultrashort (~ 10 ps) pulses of light in the visible spectral range.
we have demonstrated the possibility to generate ultrashort spontaneous pulses by quantum dots coupled to a microcavity and we have studied their properties in detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel concepts for quantum photonics and the generation of novel quantum states of light.
the study of quantum dots (QD) in microcavities and the generation of ultrashort spontaneous pulses in such a system.
the development of novel quantum optical devices based on the integration of quantum dots in optical microcavities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated the generation of ultrashort pulses of spontaneous emission from QDs in a switched optical cavity.

this work demonstrates the generation of ultrashort spontaneous emissions pulses from QD ensembles in switched optical microcavities, and that this technique could open the way to new applications in the field ultrafast optical imaging and in quantum photonics.
we have demonstrated that the emission of an ensemble of quantum dots can be used as a broadband internal source to generate ultrashort pulses in a switched microcavity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we can control the emission of a single QD by the switching of a microcavity.
the QDs are the source of the emission, the micropillar is the cavity that confines the emission and the switching is the mechanism that controls the emission into the fundamental mode of the cavity.

we have demonstrated a new type of ultrafast optical switch based on a microcavity, which allows to generate ultra-short (~10ps) light pulses by a pulsed injection of free charge carrier in the microcavity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QD ensemble can be seen as a broadband internal coherent light source for the micropillar, which can be switched at will by a simple external optical pulse.
it opens the way towards a novel type of quantum photonic device, based on the interaction of QDs with a switched optical microresonator.

the emission of a quantum system into an optical microcavity can be controlled on a picosecond time-scale by the cavity mode itself, opening the way to the development of ultra-fast cavity quantum optics.
